scope: Read-only checkpoint matrix analysis; no model instantiation, tokens, GELU evaluation, forward pass, performance evaluation, or SSH.

calculation.arithmetic: CPU float64 read from original stored tensors; no writes to checkpoint
calculation.key_value_self_alignment: cosine(W_in[i,:],W_out[:,i]) for each of2048 matched neurons
calculation.ln_adjusted_key: W_in[i,:] @ diag(gamma) @ P, gamma is post_attention_layernorm.weight, P=I-11^T/512
calculation.raw_ungated_map: W_out @ W_in (identity-GELU surrogate, not the true MLP Jacobian)
calculation.ln_adjusted_ungated_map: W_out @ W_in @ diag(gamma) @ P; excludes input-dependent inverse LayerNorm standard deviation
calculation.attention_map: O_h @ V_h, adjusted with the attention input LayerNorm gain/centering, matching prior weight-analysis.json
calculation.map_overlap: Normalized Frobenius inner product; compares matrix geometry without activation covariance
calculation.actual_local_derivative_caveat: Actual derivative includes W_out @ diag(GELU_prime(preactivation)) @ W_in and the complete input-dependent LayerNorm Jacobian. GELU is not a fixed0/1 gate; its derivative may be negative or greater than1.
calculation.normalized_key_input_coupling: ||K_m G_h||_F / (||K_m||_F ||G_h||_F), where K_m=W_in_m diag(gamma_m) P and G_h=O_h V_h diag(gamma_h) P. Excludes GELU, variance scaling, attention routing and activation covariance; not a measured gate change.

limitations: Biases shift GELU operating points; an ungated product can hide or invent cancellations among neuron contributions.
Global self-alignment distributions do not identify which neurons fire on validation tokens or on recurrent feedback.
LayerNorm removes a changing radial component and rescales inputs by token-dependent variance; fixed gain/centering alone is incomplete.
Attention-map overlap omits attention routing, Q/K biases, rotary positions, softmax and cross-token mixing; MLPs operate tokenwise.
Different layers see different residual distributions; cross-layer matrix similarity is not functional equivalence.
Concurrent same-layer head and MLP repeats are parallel in the executor: the head repeat does not enter that MLP repeat input.

bounded_hypotheses.name: head4.3 conditions MLP4 recurrence
bounded_hypotheses.status: unmeasured hypothesis; not a predicted improvement
bounded_hypotheses.other_counts: All head counts1 and all other MLP counts1.
controls: Ordinary sequence with head4.3 count2 and MLP4 count2 (parallel control).
bounded_hypotheses.reason: Head4.3 already has measured recurrent benefit. Its adjusted map overlap with MLP4 is only0.0040, so direct cancellation is unsupported; inserting it before layer4 tests changed GELU inputs instead. Normalized key-input coupling is0.04043, nonzero but not exceptional among MLPs.

bounded_hypotheses.name: MLP1 repeat with a later opposing head map
bounded_hypotheses.status: low-priority unmeasured counterbalance probe; overlap is modest
controls: Head5.3 count2 without the extra MLP1 application.
bounded_hypotheses.reason: MLP1 was the least harmful single MLP repeat, and head5.3 is its most opposing attention map (adjusted cosine−0.08244). This can test a later residual correction; it cannot condition MLP1 in the same traversal, and attention routing/downstream layers prevent a cancellation claim.

bounded_hypotheses.name: one extra pass through layers1 and2
bounded_hypotheses.status: low-priority unmeasured cross-layer interaction probe, not evidence of a key/value chain
bounded_hypotheses.other_counts: All heads and MLP counts1 within each visit.
controls: Existing individual layer1 and layer2 repeat results.
bounded_hypotheses.reason: MLP1/MLP2 have the strongest adjusted ungated-map alignment among MLP pairs (0.24971), with mostly negative individual key/value self-alignment. An extra block tests whether feedback saturates or compounds those related transformations. Whole-layer repetition also repeats attention and shared biases, so this does not isolate MLPs.

mlp1_vs_mlp5_assessment.interpretation: MLP5 has larger output weights, somewhat larger ungated adjusted map, and much larger affine surrogate output offset. MLP1 has predominantly negative affine preactivation offsets; MLP5 has predominantly positive ones. These make different repetition sensitivities plausible but do not establish activation gating, realized output sizes, or causation of perplexity changes.

separate_existing_activation_evidence.scope: Diagnostic only; one full-context forward, not an evaluation or perplexity estimate.
separate_existing_activation_evidence.read_only_use: Produced remotely by parent; this analysis only read the saved JSON and checked RMS/cosine arithmetic. No local forward pass.
separate_existing_activation_evidence.interpretation: On this one prefix window, MLP1/2 second applications shrink and change direction, while MLP5 second output grows and closely aligns with its first. This supports lower priority for MLP5 recurrence and bounded additional MLP1/2 probes; it is not a full-sample loss explanation or evidence of stable convergence.
